text.p: Bally Total Fitness Holding Corp said Wednesday it adopted a change in accounting methods, conforming its revenue recognition to that of the service industry in general.
The restatement has no impact on cash flows, liquidity or the strategic direction of the business, the company said.
"The company believes the new accounting will yield more stable and predictable results over longer time periods," said Lee Hillman, president & chief executive.
"The new accounting method will minimize seasonality of the company's new membership revenues, deferring recognition during the company's peak first quarter to later periods," he added.

As a result of the change, the previously reported results for the year ended December 31, 1996 improved by $16.3 million to a loss of $19.2 million or $1.58 per share. Deferred revenues on the balance sheet at December 31, 1996 increased a net $192.4 million with an offsetting decrease of stockholders' equity to $24.2 million.

For the quarter ended March 31, 1997, previously reported net income decreased $8.2 million resulting in a loss of $5.7 million or $0.46 per share, compared with a restated loss of $12.0 million or $0.98 per share for the first quarter of 1996.

Bally said it is following a "deferral method" with respect to the timing of recognition of initial membership fees. Revenues from membership initiation fees are spread ratably over the expected membership life. Previously, the company generally recognized revenues from membership initiation fees at the time the memberships were sold.
Bally Total Fitness is a commercial operator of fitness centers in the United States with about four million members and 320 facilities in 27 states and Canada.
